summary: This roadmap supplies the nonordinary complex special values and normalized elliptic-unit reciprocity needed at an inert prime of an imaginary quadratic field. It proves the auxiliary-character, root-number, conductor, period and coefficient comparisons behind the local optimal-unit argument. Its main unit theorem specializes Finis at an inert valuation prime without assuming ordinary CM reduction. General elliptic units, Hecke characters and Lubin–Tate theory retain their existing owners.

nodes.title: An integral elliptic CM period
nodes.statement: For a CM Gross Q-curve E/H of type (1,0), good at every prime above the inert p, choose an actual smooth integral Weierstrass model near p and its Néron differential ω. After moving to a conjugate in the ideal-class orbit, choose Ω∈C× with the integration lattice of (E,ω) equal to Ω O_K. The normalized central value A_S(η;E,ω,Ω) is Ω⁻¹ L_S(η,1), a complex number. Its algebraicity for η=barφχ with χ of finite order, and hence its p-adic avatar under the fixed embeddings, is a consequence of the elliptic-unit reciprocity law (NCM.1/elliptic-reciprocity, Kato's Proposition 15.9); it is not part of this construction, and no map C→C_p is used. Here S is a finite set of finite primes and L_S deletes their native local factors.
hypotheses: K is imaginary quadratic; p≥5 is inert, p∤h_K, and p is prime to the conductor f of φ.
E/H realizes φ∘N_(H/K), is a Q-curve, and the fixed embeddings of algebraic numbers into C and C_p agree on K.
The ideal class of the lattice is made principal by changing E within its conjugate CM orbit; Ω is then a choice up to O_K×.
proofSteps: Import the CM curve and its good model from CM.4, and its analytic ideal-lattice realization from CM.1. Move the lattice class by the inverse ideal class using CM reciprocity.

Integrate the actual invariant differential to obtain Ω O_K and define the quotient in C. Its algebraic meaning is read off later from Kato's Proposition 15.9, whose dual-exponential image lies in the algebraic de Rham line S(φ)⊗_K K′; the GL₂/Q period interface of AL.5 is not used.
Retain the differential and both embeddings as data. No ordinary multiplicative formal-group trivialization or Katz p-adic period is part of this construction.
acceptance: The lattice equality is an output and Ω is nonzero.
Every assertion of p-adic integrality refers to an algebraic normalized value and a specified valuation.

nodes.title: Canonical root number at a split dyadic prime
nodes.statement: If φ is a canonical Gross character of an imaginary quadratic K with fundamental discriminant −D and 2 split in K, then W(φ)=W(barφ)=(2/D)=+1. Canonical means the CM.4 predicate: conjugation equivariance, signed principal values and conductor supported at ramified primes. The split condition forces D odd and D≡7 mod8. This theorem is conditional on the supplied canonical character; it does not reconstruct its existence.
hypotheses: The Hecke ideal character has infinity type (1,0), its idelic avatar has archimedean value z⁻¹, and its unitary normalization has central point 1/2.
Use the standard global additive character and self-dual local measures from AL.1.
proofSteps: Import the canonical conductor and rational-principal-character identities. At a ramified odd rational q the conductor and different both have exponent one.

Apply the imported local epsilon formula. In Rohrlich’s standard additive-character convention the complex factor is −i and each ramified odd q contributes i^δ_q (2/q) times the product of (q/r) over other ramified r, where δ_q=0 for q≡1 mod4 and δ_q=1 for q≡3 mod4. To compare an opposite Fourier convention in AL.1, replace ψ_v by ψ_v(−·): at the unitary center the local epsilon changes by the local character at −1. The global product of these factors is one because the character is trivial on K×. Thus individual archimedean phases must be converted together with every finite factor.
Multiply over q|D. Quadratic reciprocity cancels the powers of i and the pairwise residue symbols, leaving (2/D). Conjugation reindexes the ideal L-series, so barφ has the same sign.
acceptance: K=Q(sqrt(−7)) gives sign +1; the canonical character for Q(sqrt(−11)) has sign −1 and fails the dyadic split hypothesis.
No statement is exported for even D from this calculation.

sources.match: The full local calculation expresses the canonical sign as the quadratic symbol (2/D).
The auxiliary split-at-2 field is used precisely to make the canonical sign positive.

nodes.title: An auxiliary split prime away from p−1
nodes.statement: For K imaginary quadratic, p≥5 inert in K, and a finite set S of rational primes containing those dividing p h_K N(f), there are infinitely many rational primes l∉S with l≥5, l split in K and l not congruent to 1 modulo p. In particular p∤(l−1), as required by BKO (3.3).
hypotheses: p is unramified in K; f is a fixed nonzero ideal.
proofSteps: Because p is unramified in K, the quadratic field K cannot be the quadratic subfield of Q(μ_p), whose discriminant is divisible by p. Hence K and Q(μ_p) are linearly disjoint.
Choose a nonidentity a in (Z/p)× and the element (1,a) of the Galois group of the compositum over Q. Import Chebotarev with its positive-density-to-infinitude consequence.
Remove S and the primes below 5. The selected Frobenius splits in K and gives l≡a modp.
acceptance: Merely choosing a split prime does not imply p∤(l−1).
The finite exclusion includes the full norm of f and h_K; the surviving set remains infinite.

sources.match: The auxiliary prime must split, avoid the conductor and class number, and have l−1 prime to p.

nodes.title: Finite characters in the auxiliary anticyclotomic tower
nodes.statement: Let K_l^ac/K be the anticyclotomic Z_l-extension inside the ring-class tower. X_l is its set of continuous finite-image characters Γ_l→Qbar×, equivalently the union of the character groups of its finite quotients. The ideal avatar and p-adic avatar use the fixed embeddings and arithmetic Artin map. For ν≠1 write order(ν)=l^r, r≥1, and cond(ν)=l^m O_K with m=r+1. For ν=1 set m=0. Write L[r] for the degree-l^r layer through which ν factors; conductor indices and layer indices are never identified.
hypotheses: l≥5 splits in K and l∤h_K N(f); the two primes over l use the rational ring-class modulus l^m O_K.
Γ_l is supplied by class field theory; changing a topological generator changes coordinate descriptions, not X_l.
proofSteps: Import the ring-class idele quotient and its pro-l part. Its principal-unit anticyclotomic quotient at depth m has order l^(m−1), since l∤h_K and l∤#O_K×.
Use the Hecke/ray-character equivalence to form the primitive ideal character and its actual conductor.
For each finite quotient evaluate its group algebra with MonoidAlgebra.lift ν. In particular a basis vector [g] maps to ν(g), without inversion.
acceptance: The first nontrivial wild character has conductor l², not l.
Conjugation on the tower sends ν to ν⁻¹; the prime p O_K acts trivially because it is principal in every prime-to-p order.

nodes.title: The CM dual and Tate-twist dictionary
nodes.statement: Let T_φ be the rank-one integral p-adic realization of the ideal character φ, and put T_φ^∨(1)=Hom_R(T_φ,R)(1). At every prime above p of H this has the de Rham line identified with R[1/p]⊗coLie(E), generated by ω. In Kato’s notation ψ=φ has idelic type (−1,0), V(ψ) has the inverse φ-action, and V(ψ)(1) is T_φ^∨(1)[1/p]. The normalized Betti vector is γ=per_φ(ω)/Ω. Under this dictionary the analytic character in Proposition 15.9 is barφ times the direct finite character, not φ, barφ⁻¹, or barφ times an inverse finite character.
hypotheses: φ, E, ω and Ω satisfy the period datum; R is the integer ring of a finite extension of Φ containing the p-adic character values.
Coefficient and representation duals are R-linear; the Tate twist is the actual cyclotomic representation.
proofSteps: Import CM.4’s ideal/Frobenius and idelic-infinity conventions, then compare the r=1 case of CZ.1/cm-hecke-realization.
Identify the inverse-action cohomological realization and its Tate twist using the CM comparison; compare its cotangent generator with the chosen ω.
Track Kato’s complex conjugation on ψ in the analytic expression. Fourier reindexing is done after this comparison and introduces no extra conjugation on ν or χ.
acceptance: At a good prime a, the dual-twisted arithmetic Frobenius is N(a)/φ(a), as dictated by the dual and Tate operations.
The displayed BKO (3.4) has barφ χ on its right side, with χ direct; this is checked against the PDF image.

sources.match: The cohomological realization uses the inverse character, followed by a Tate twist, and the L-function uses the conjugated Hecke character.
The local cotangent line and normalized Betti vector fix the precise dual/Tate dictionary.

nodes.title: The integral BKO elliptic-unit class
nodes.statement: For the period datum and γ=per_φ(ω)/Ω, specialize the shared elliptic-unit zeta element to a norm-compatible class z_a in H¹(K(a),T_φ^∨(1)), for every admissible modulus a divisible by f and supported on f,p and an auxiliary split l. The classes are the Kummer images of the shared theta-distribution element, with its smoothing factors removed in the φ-component only after proving those factors invertible on the specified integral lattice. Its rationalization agrees with Kato’s z_a^(p)(γ). For p-power increases of a the transition is corestriction, with the native Euler factors at newly introduced primes retained.
hypotheses: The integer coefficient ring R contains the φ-values and the chosen Betti vector is integral in the specified realization.
The exact smoothing-denominator/lattice assertion is supplier obligation G1; Kato’s fraction-module element by itself is insufficient.
proofSteps: Import CZ.0’s theta distribution, elliptic-unit module and tower Kummer map, then the rational reciprocity theorem CZ.1.

Calculate the smoothing operator on the rank-one φ-component, prove its denominators are units in the chosen lattice, and identify the inverse-action Tate lattice through NCM.0/dual-tate-convention. This is the unresolved integral supplier boundary, not an asserted consequence of localization.

Sufficient route for the BKO application (recorded under G1): only the image after the ν-evaluation, the augmentation over Gal(H/K) and the Δ-invariant projection has to be integral. Under the twist (3.5) Kato's smoothing factor N(a)−σ_a becomes N(a)−φ(a)σ_a (Kato (15.9.2)). Take a=(α) with α≡1 mod 6·f·l^(m+1) and α≡2 mod p. On that component σ_a acts through ν(a)=1 and a pro-p element, so the factor reduces to N(a)−φ(a)=α(ᾱ−1), a p-adic unit; it is therefore invertible in the local Iwasawa algebra there, and Kato's (15.6.3) gives integrality of the projected element without the full lattice statement.
Use the native Kummer map and its norm/corestriction compatibility to obtain the integral family and compare its rationalization with Kato’s normalized γ element.
acceptance: The output is an actual integral continuous-cohomology class, not an existential variable chosen to satisfy reciprocity.
At a prime newly added to the modulus the Euler-system relation is checked before restricting to the fixed-support p-power tower.

sources.match: The unsmoothed object is initially in a fraction module; the r=1 specialization and γ normalization determine its rational image.
BKO uses an integral class with this normalization, which requires a lattice comparison beyond the rational formula.
The smoothed element (N(a)−σ_a)z is integral, and after twisting by the CM character the smoothing factor reads N(a)−ψ(a)σ_a.

nodes.title: Direct-character dual-exponential reciprocity
nodes.statement: For the normalized class at a ray level K(gp^n) with g divisible by f, and a finite-order character χ of its Galois group, the χ-weighted localized dual exponential is Ω⁻¹ L_{pg}(barφ χ,1)·ω: sum over σ of χ(σ) exp*_{p}(loc_p(z_a^σ)) equals that value in the common algebraic coefficient/de Rham line after the stated embeddings. The finite sum includes the semilocal places and the trace used by the native localization; no implicit inverse-character idempotent is inserted.
hypotheses: χ factors through the chosen finite ray level and the period, γ and coefficient lattice are those of NCM.0 and NCM.1.
L_{pg} deletes exactly the primes dividing p and g. For g=f this is L_{pf}; for auxiliary ν use g=f l^m with the actual conductor exponent m.
proofSteps: Apply CZ.1/cm-elliptic-reciprocity to the rationalized zeta class. Its proof boundary is Kato’s generalized Coleman reciprocity and Eisenstein evaluation, already owned by CZ.1.
Identify the inverse-action/Tate-twist realization, then identify γ with per_φ(ω)/Ω; use the trace pairing normalization of the dual exponential.
Expand the character specialization as the direct weighted sum and track each finite Euler factor. Equality of the integral classes is not inferred from this rational equality.
acceptance: For χ=1 the Euler factor at inert p is retained: it is 1+1/p for the conjugate weight-one character at s=1 and is not a p-unit.
For ν or χ nonreal, replacing the direct character by its inverse changes the target value and is not accepted as a convention-free equality.

sources.locator: Equation (3.4), p.952, visually checked conjugation bar
sources.match: Only φ is conjugated in the analytic character; χ is evaluated directly.
The comparison is obtained from generalized Coleman reciprocity and the specialized Eisenstein expression.

nodes.title: Twisting the norm-compatible Kummer tower
nodes.statement: Over F_∞=K(fp^∞), where the φ-adic torsion representation is trivialized by its actual torsion points, the native Kummer identification gives an R-linear comparison between lim_cor H¹(F_n,Z_p(1)) tensored with T_φ^∨ and lim_cor H¹(F_n,T_φ^∨(1)). The first term uses the p-adic completion of the appropriate S-unit groups, with the exact finite-S Kummer correction retained. The comparison is equivariant for Gal(F_∞/K) with the diagonal action and agrees with BKO (3.5).
hypotheses: T_φ is finite free of rank one over R; choose a compatible basis only to express the map.
Use continuous inverse limits and completed coefficients; no assertion identifies an unrestricted algebraic tensor of the whole unit group with its p-adic completion.
proofSteps: Use the finite-S native Kummer theorem at each finite level and the inverse-action CM representation.

Work first modulo p^k and pass to the cofinal tower levels on which T_φ/p^k is trivial. Apply the native continuous Iwasawa/Shapiro twist comparison, then take its justified coefficient and norm inverse limits. Finite freeness makes tensoring a finite direct-sum operation, so it commutes with the relevant limit once the continuous-cohomology comparison is supplied. This is not an assertion that T_φ is trivial at every finite level.
Check the descent action explicitly: the coefficient factor transforms by φ⁻¹, so the equivariant comparison has the asserted diagonal action. Basis change multiplies both sides by the same unit.
acceptance: The map commutes with localization and corestriction, so it may be used before taking the semilocal ν projection.
Without triviality of the representation on F_∞, the untwisted Kummer map alone gives no such identification.

sources.match: The comparison is an inverse-limit tensor twist, not a new definition of the cohomology group.

nodes.title: Compatibility of reciprocity with period changes
nodes.statement: For fixed ω, replacing Ω by uΩ and γ by u⁻¹γ, with u a unit in the common integral coefficient field, multiplies z_a and both sides of the reciprocity identity by u⁻¹. Replacing instead the good differential by vω and the period by vΩ, with v∈H× a unit at the chosen place above p (so that vω is again an algebraic differential and Néron-normalized there), leaves γ=per_φ(ω)/Ω and z_a unchanged; the scalar normalized value becomes v⁻¹A, and its product with the de Rham generator vω is unchanged. Thus the p-unit assertion is independent of the allowed choices, with the two changes distinguished.
hypotheses: The new period still represents the same principal lattice in the first case only when u is an allowed lattice unit; algebraic renormalizations outside this case must also change the Betti normalization explicitly.
All scalars are interpreted through the common algebraic embeddings.
proofSteps: Use linearity of the period map, shared zeta construction and dual exponential.
Compute the two transformations separately; cancel v only in the product of the normalized scalar and differential.
Unit valuations show invariance of the unit property; a nonunit differential rescaling fails the good-model hypothesis.
acceptance: The differential change by 2 keeps the cohomology class fixed while changing the normalized scalar by 1/2.
A period-only change by an allowed root of unity changes the class and scalar together.

sources.match: Tracking both ω and Ω distinguishes changes of the differential from changes of Betti normalization.

nodes.title: The torsion and ring-class compositum
nodes.statement: For n≥0 and r≥0 define F_n=H(E[p^(n+1)]) and M_(n,r)=F_n L[r] inside the fixed algebraic closure of K. For ν of exact order l^r with r≥1 use its actual conductor l^m, m=r+1; M_(n,r) is contained in the ray field K(f l^m p^(n+1)), while for ν=1 use m=0. The maps between these fields give the actual corestriction maps on continuous Kummer cohomology. The local field Φ_n is the completion of F_n at the chosen place above p, with Φ_0 the first p-torsion level.
hypotheses: E/H has CM by O_K, satisfies the Shimura condition and has good reduction above p; p∤h_K N(f).
The fields and embeddings are compatible throughout the tower, with Φ=K_p the unramified quadratic extension of Q_p.
proofSteps: Form composita of the actual CM torsion and anticyclotomic class fields. Import CM reciprocity to place the torsion field in the ray field and combine it with the conductor calculation for ν.
Define finite-level cohomological transition maps by restriction of the native field extension/corestriction functor, not by multiplying a proposed generator by a formal degree.
Localize after corestriction. Use the disjointness and splitting theorems below to compare this with the semilocal product.
acceptance: The auxiliary conductor and the field-layer index differ by one for nontrivial characters.

nodes.title: Ramification proves linear disjointness
nodes.statement: F_n and L[r] are linearly disjoint over K, so the multiplication map F_n⊗_K L[r]→M_(n,r) is an isomorphism. This remains true when l divides p²−1. In fact their intersection has l-power degree, is unramified at l because the torsion field is, and is unramified away from l because L[r]/K is; hence it is an everywhere-unramified abelian l-extension of K and is trivial since l∤h_K.

nodes.title: Auxiliary twists preserve the root number

Both ideals are stable under complex conjugation (f by the conjugation identity, 𝔡_K=(√−D)), and an anticyclotomic character of odd order is trivial on a conjugation-stable ideal b, since ν(b)=ν(b̄)=ν(b)⁻¹.

nodes.statement: Let χ be a nontrivial finite-order character of the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension of K, of exact order p^n with n≥1 and actual conductor p^c O_K, c=n+1. nodes.title: The weight-one Finis family
nodes.statement: For canonical φ and ν∈X_l, define the ideal character λ_ν(a)=barφ(a)ν(a)/N(a)=φ(a)⁻¹ν(a), away from its conductor. In idelic notation multiply the avatar of barφν by the global norm absolute value |·|_A, whose ideal avatar is N⁻¹; the archimedean component is z. Thus λ has Finis’s idelic infinity type (−1,0), is self-dual in his sense λ=λ*, and L(0,λ)=L(barφν,1). Finis’s tower prime q is our split l, while his valuation prime is our inert p. The complex period is the one obtained from the same good CM differential, with its ambiguity restricted to p-adic units.

Choose Finis’s auxiliary CM curve and differential to be exactly our E/H and ω. His good-reduction condition is imposed at the valuation prime, which is our inert p, and permits this same pair. Both definitions then use the identical principal lattice Ω O_K, with only O_K× ambiguity. Thus no ordinary p-adic period or unproved nonunit period ratio is inserted.

nodes.title: Rohrlich's lattice-point bound for p-adic directions
nodes.statement: Let P be a finite set of rational primes and, for each p∈P, let (α_p,β_p)∈Z_p², not both zero, be elements algebraic over Q. For a positive integer q divisible only by primes of P and t>0, let M(q,t) be the number of (u,v)∈Z² with uβ_p−vα_p≡0 mod qZ_p and uβ_p−vα_p≠0 for every p∈P, and max(|u|,|v|)≤t. Then (1) for each fixed c<1/2, M(q,q^c)=0 for all sufficiently large q; (2) there are absolute constants d>1/2 and s<1/2 (for example d=11/20 and s=7/16) with M(q,q^d)<q^s for all sufficiently large q.
hypotheses: α_p, β_p∈Z_p are algebraic over Q and not both zero; q has prime factors only in P.
The congruence has modulus qZ_p and the boxes have sides q^c and q^d; Jia v1 §4 prints Z_p and q⁻¹ there (E3, E4).
proofSteps: Ridout's homogeneous inequality: for algebraic γ_p∈Q_p and κ>2 there is k>0 with ∏_(p∈P)|u−vγ_p|_p>k·max(|u|,|v|)^(−κ) whenever the left side is nonzero. Derive it from the p-adic subspace theorem with n=2: take the forms X, Y at ∞ and X−γ_pY, Y at each p∈P, each pair in general position. A primitive (u,v) violating the bound makes the double product at most max(|u|,|v|)^(2−κ), because |v|_∞∏_(p∈P)|v|_p≤|v|. So such solutions lie on finitely many lines through 0, each with at most two primitive points. Multiplying (u,v) by n≠0 keeps the bound, since ∏_(p∈P)|n|_p≥|n|⁻¹.

Part (1): choose j with β_p+jα_p≠0 for every p, put γ_p=α_p(β_p+jα_p)⁻¹ and choose κ with c<1/κ<1/2. A pair in M(q,q^c) has ∏_p|uβ_p−vα_p|_p≤q⁻¹ and max(|u|,|v|)≤q^c. The Ridout bound gives ∏_p|uβ_p−vα_p|_p>k₁q^(−κc), which is impossible for large q since κc<1.

Part (2): fix 1/2<d<3/5 and 5d/2−1<s<1/2. Cover the box of side q^d by at most ([2q^(d−c)]+1)² squares of side q^c. If M(q,q^d)≥q^s, two points of one square differ by a pair in M(q,q^c) unless the difference lies on one of the lines uβ_p=vα_p. Part (1) excludes the first case for large q. In the second, a positive proportion of the points lies on one rational line; a Dirichlet-principle subdivision along that line and the rational-slope case give a contradiction (Rohrlich, pp.403–407).
acceptance: For P={p} and a rational direction (α_p,β_p)=(a,b), |ub−va| is a nonzero integer divisible by q, so M(q,q^d)=0 for any fixed d<1 once q is large.
With modulus Z_p instead of qZ_p every pair in the box off the finitely many direction lines is counted, and part (1) fails.

sources.match: Section 3 is self-contained: the vanishing count follows from Ridout's theorem, and the q^s bound from a covering by squares, the vanishing count and a rational-line case.

nodes.title: The CM Galois-average nonvanishing estimate
nodes.statement: Let K be any imaginary quadratic field and φ an algebraic ideal Hecke character of type (1,0) satisfying φ(bar a)=barφ(a), equivalently φ((n))=κ_K(n)n on rational integers prime to its conductor. Fix a finite set P of rational primes and let ρ range over the finite-order characters of Gal(L_P/K), where L_P is the union of the ring class fields of K whose conductors are divisible only by primes of P, with W(φρ)=+1. Partition the family by its finite rational conductor support R, and fix one such support. Write η=φρ, f(η)=sqrt(N cond(η)), and κ_R for the quadratic Dirichlet character of K induced to a modulus containing R, extended by zero at every prime of R. As f(η) tends to infinity within this fixed-support family, the average of L(1,η^σ) over the K-embeddings σ of the character-value field tends to 2L(1,κ_R), which is nonzero. There are only finitely many supports R. The statement includes arbitrary class number.
hypotheses: Use the conjugation-stable primitive conductor and the action of Aut(C/K) on character values.

The average is purely analytic: each η^σ is again a type-(1,0) character with the same conductor and root number. The algebraicity input that makes a single vanishing value force the whole average to vanish is used only in NCM.5/central-nonvanishing.
proofSteps: Partition by the finite conductor support R as in Jia's p.4 reduction. Use the sign-positive approximate functional equation with the native primitive character extended by zero at its conductor. The rational-ideal contribution is restricted to integers prime to R (Rohrlich 1984, p.386, defines κ to vanish on R) and tends to 2L(1,κ_R), with A=sqrt(|disc K|)/(2π). Equivalently it is 2L(1,κ_K) times the finite nonzero factors 1−κ_K(q)/q for q∈R. The nonconjugation-stable ideal contribution has exponential cutoff exp(−N(a)/(Af)).

For σ∈Aut(C/K), η^σ is again a Hecke character of type (1,0) with the same conductor and with η^σ((n))=κ_K(n)n. Its root number equals W(η): write W through the explicit Gauss-sum formula and let σ act on the Gauss sum (Jia (2.13)–(2.18), pp.5–6; Rohrlich 1984 §4, p.407). So the whole Galois orbit lies in the sign-positive family and the average (2.20)–(2.22) is formed inside it.

For N_η(t), the count of nonstable ideals of norm≤t with nonzero averaged character, use the trace-of-roots-of-unity criterion (Jia Lemma 1). Fix an ideal-class representative a_0 with a_0^h=(w_0); write a=(w)a_0 and keep the h-th root of w_0. Jia's Main Lemma turns nonzero trace into finitely many simultaneous p-adic direction congruences modulo q(η), with q(η) comparable to f(η). Lemma 3 rescales the directions to algebraic ones. This class-group step cannot be replaced by the class-number-one principal-ideal argument.

Apply NCM.5/rohrlich-lattice-count through Jia's transfer (Propositions 3 and 4, pp.15–17): N_η(t) is bounded by finitely many counts M(q(η),k·t^(1/2)). Hence N_η(f^a)=0 eventually for each a<1, and N_η(f^b)<f^r for some b>1, r<1/2.

Choose 2r<a<1. The short sum is zero; the middle sum is O(f^(r−a/2)); polynomial ideal counting and the exponential cutoff make the tail tend to zero. The induced quadratic κ_R is nontrivial, so import the pinned Dirichlet L(1) nonvanishing theorem for this actual fixed-support main term. Finitely many supports give the finite-exception result for the full family.
acceptance: The h-th root and finite-coset direction corrections survive when h_K>1; no E/Q hypothesis is inserted.
The estimates are ineffective; no explicit list or conductor bound for exceptions is exported.

For K=Q(sqrt(−7)) and a family ramified at p=5, the rational term omits multiples of 5 and its limiting Dirichlet value contains the factor 1+1/5. The primitive quadratic value without this factor is not the limiting constant.

nodes.title: Correct-sign central values are almost always nonzero
nodes.statement: For a BKO CM Gross Q-curve character φ over arbitrary imaginary quadratic K, and fixed ν∈X_l, all but finitely many finite-order characters χ of the p-anticyclotomic Z_p-extension with W(barφνχ)=+1 satisfy L(barφνχ,1)≠0. For nontrivial χ of conductor p^c this is the parity (−1)^c W(φ)=+1. Every finite-deleted value L_S(barφνχ,1) is then nonzero as well: at an unramified prime the removed Euler polynomial has parameter of complex absolute value N(q)⁻¹/²<1, and a ramified rank-one prime has factor 1. The theorem provides no derivative assertion in the opposite-sign case.
hypotheses: p≥5 is inert, p∤h_K N(f), and ν is fixed, so P={p,l} and the conductor outside p is bounded.
Vanishing at s=1 is transported along Aut(C/K) by the weight-two CM newform attached to the character and the coefficient-embedding comparison of normalized critical values of newforms.
proofSteps: Reindex the ideal series by a↦bar a: L(barφνχ,s)=L(φν⁻¹χ⁻¹,s). Apply the average theorem to the type-(1,0) character φ and the finite character ρ=ν⁻¹χ⁻¹, rather than assigning type (1,0) to barφ. The family χ↦ν⁻¹χ⁻¹ is injective and has unbounded p-conductor; its root number is unchanged under this equality of completed L-functions.

If L(1,η)=0 for η=φν⁻¹χ⁻¹, let θ_η be the weight-two CM newform with L(θ_η,s)=L(η,s) (CZ.5/cm-newform-characterization, case k=2). For σ∈Aut(C/K) its coefficient conjugate θ_η^σ is θ_(η^σ). The coefficient-embedding comparison carries the period-normalized value L(θ_η,1)/Ω⁺ to L(θ_(η^σ),1)/Ω⁺, so every L(1,η^σ) vanishes and the Galois average is zero (Jia p.2, citing Shimura). The nonzero limiting main term of NCM.5/averaged-value-limit excludes this for sufficiently large conductor.

There are only finitely many χ of bounded conductor. Combine this with the parity theorem. For any finite Euler deletion, the unramified local parameter at s=1 has complex absolute value N(q)⁻¹/²<1 and therefore its polynomial does not vanish; the ramified factor is 1. Thus the same finite exceptional set works for every fixed finite deletion set.
acceptance: Agboola–Howard Proposition 3.1 is a class-number-one cross-check, not the general-K proof.
Wrong-sign characters still have zero value; the almost-all quantifier ranges over the correct-sign family.

nodes.title: Unramified coefficients for the canonical family
nodes.statement: For canonical φ with p∤h_K D and ν∈X_l, the field Φ(φ,ν) generated over Φ by the p-adic values of φ on ideals prime to f and the values of ν is a finite unramified extension; let W be its ring of integers. The rank-one realization T_φ and the auxiliary evaluation are defined over W. The normalized value A_ν=Ω⁻¹L_f(barφν,1) lies in a finite unramified extension of Φ, so valuation zero makes it a unit of the ring of integers of any unramified coefficient field containing it.
hypotheses: The conductor’s finite character has the canonical signed-principal values; an arbitrary ramified coefficient realization is outside this assertion.
All ideal-class representatives and principal generators are chosen prime to p and f.
proofSteps: For a class representative a of order d|h_K, write a^d=(α) with α prime to p and f. The canonical identity gives φ(a)^d=±α. Since p∤d, X^d−(±α) has unit derivative at its unit roots, and its splitting field over Φ is unramified. Principal values lie in K up to the canonical sign. Finitely many representatives generate the value field.
The values of ν have l-power order prime to p, hence lie in finite unramified extensions. The chosen good CM curve has coefficients in H, whose completion at p is Φ.

For the value: apply NCM.1/elliptic-reciprocity at level g=f·l^m with the character ν, which is trivial on the p-power part of Gal(K(gp^n)/K). The ν-weighted dual-exponential sum is then invariant under Gal(K(gp^n)/K(g)), so it lies in W[1/p]⊗coLie(E)⊗_K K(g). Kato's Proposition 15.9 places it in the algebraic de Rham line, and K(g)/K is unramified above p. Hence Ω⁻¹L_(pg)(barφν,1) lies in a finite unramified extension of Φ. The p-Euler factor 1+1/p is rational, and the l-factors are 1 for ν≠1 (NCM.4/ramified-euler-factors).
acceptance: The p∤h_K hypothesis is used in the derivative of X^d−u; removing it invalidates the unramifiedness proof.
An arbitrary period rescaling by a ramified coefficient unit can preserve valuation but leaves this specified unramified normalization.
For ν=1 the descent uses level f and keeps the p-Euler factor 1+1/p separate; it is a rational number, not a unit.

nodes.title: Compare scalar and tensor character kernels
nodes.statement: Let F=Φ_n be the totally ramified division field in C_p and U=Frac(W) a finite unramified extension of Φ as in the canonical coefficient theorem. The multiplication map F⊗_Φ U→C_p is injective. Therefore for every χ of the finite anticyclotomic quotient with values in F and every finite family x_σ∈F⊗_Φ U, the literal tensor sum Σσ χ(σ)x_σ vanishes iff its scalar image in C_p vanishes. The same implication holds for the integral tensor after its flat injection into this rational tensor. It applies to any native derivative or dual-exponential evaluation landing in this tensor, without defining signed local units here.
hypotheses: χ has order at most p^n and μ_(p^(n+1))⊂Φ_n, so its values already lie in F.
Both fields use the fixed compatible embeddings, and the cohomological/derivative output must first be proved to land in the stated tensor.
This is a canonical unramified-coefficient comparison, not a result for arbitrary R in BKO §6.
proofSteps: A common subextension of a totally ramified and an unramified local extension has both properties and is trivial. Use the local Galois disjointness theorem to obtain linear disjointness.

Apply the pinned injectivity characterization of the actual tensor multiplication map; restriction of scalars gives the integral statement by flatness of the unramified coefficient ring and torsion freeness.

The character-weighted sum is an element of this tensor because χ-values lie in F. Injectivity is exactly what permits scalar vanishing to imply literal tensor vanishing. For general ramified coefficients the multiplication map can have a kernel, so the argument cannot be reused without a new hypothesis.
acceptance: If U=F is a nontrivial ramified field, a⊗1−1⊗a can be nonzero while multiplying to zero; the unramified hypothesis excludes this counterexample.
No local signed decomposition is used to prove injectivity. The output can be consumed before that decomposition.
